bugs.root_cause: domTranslations.ts's MutationObserver watches childList/characterData mutations on the WHOLE document.body subtree continuously (not just at initial mount). Any i18next text node that is inserted into the DOM AFTER the current language is already es (true for essentially every StateBlock error message, since those only mount once a useQuery settles into isError - always some time after initial page load) gets processed by translateTextNode(). getSourceText() first calls translateToEnglish(current), which does an EXACT match against REVERSE_TRANSLATIONS - a reverse dictionary built from BOTH the small hardcoded PHRASE_TRANSLATIONS map AND (critically) every single en.ts/es.ts key pair via flattenDictionaryPairs(en, es). Since the StateBlock error text IS a real, already-correct es.ts value that exactly matches its own en.ts/es.ts key pair, the reverse lookup succeeds and recovers the ENGLISH original. The translator then re-forward-translates that recovered English original via the cruder word-level PHRASE_TRANSLATIONS/GLOSSARY_TRANSLATIONS glossary (not the real es.ts value), producing a hybrid whenever the English original is a multi-word phrase that only partially glossary-matches (e.g. "Couldn't load your subscription." only matches on the single glossary word "Subscription"/"subscription"). This is the SAME underlying mechanism as bug-962/963/964 but a NEW manifestation: it does not require a hard-reload race or a hardcoded-literal gap - it happens on ANY correctly-i18next-translated text that mounts into the DOM later than the initial synchronous render pass, which describes almost every conditionally-rendered UI state (loading->error transitions, modals, async content) across the whole app, not just PageHeader.
bugs.fix: NOT fixed this session - explicitly deferred, matching 33-07's established precedent of flagging (not expanding scope to fix) broader instances of this same defect mechanism discovered outside a close-out plan's specific check boundary (the 34-08 plan's own success criteria explicitly scope the domTranslations.ts check to PageHeader title/subtitle/tab, not StateBlock body copy). A proper fix would require either (a) a global architectural hardening of domTranslations.ts itself (e.g. skip any node whose exact current text has an exact reverse-dictionary hit, since that already proves it is correctly-translated i18next content, not stale legacy DOM text needing recovery), or (b) systematically threading a StateBlock-level dataI18nSkip prop through every call site across Phases 30-36 (a much larger, multi-phase undertaking exceeding a single close-out plan's reasonable scope). Recommends option (a) as the more scalable fix - it would resolve this defect class globally without requiring per-call-site opt-in threading across dozens of files.

bugs.root_cause: These 3 PageHeader call sites (added/touched by 34-03/34-04/34-05/34-06) kept title/subtitle as HARDCODED English literal props (never wired to i18next t()) while also being given dataI18nSkip={v2} per the bug-962/963 Pitfall-1 precedent. dataI18nSkip correctly renders data-i18n-skip="true" on the h1/p once v2 (an async, hotel-store-derived flag) resolves — but LanguageSync.tsx only re-runs translateDom()/re-installs the MutationObserver when the LANGUAGE itself changes (useEffect deps: [language]), not when an unrelated v2 flag deep in a child component resolves later. Root cause A (component-mount race): on a hard reload while the persisted language is already es, translateDom() fires once on mount BEFORE the async v2/data-i18n-skip resolves, permanently hybrid-mangling the hardcoded literal into the WeakMap-cached textOriginals with no later re-check (React bails out of touching the text node again since the JSX literal itself never changes). Root cause B (the more common real-world path, confirmed live): once v2 IS already resolved (data-i18n-skip="true" present) BEFORE the user ever toggles language, dataI18nSkip correctly and permanently blocks the legacy translator from ever touching this node — but since these 3 strings were never given a real i18next translation to replace it, blocking the legacy (imperfect but partially-working) translator left them with literally NO translation at all, worse than doing nothing.

bugs.error_message: Spanish UI shows garbled/mixed-language text (e.g. PMCompletionModal title renders "Complete PM Horario" instead of "Completar programa de PM"), and worse: raw USER DATA gets mangled by word-substitution (a PM schedule literally named "HVAC Filter Check" rendered as "HVAC Filtrar Check" in the Spanish UI). React also logs a hydration mismatch error in the console when this fires.
bugs.root_cause: This project has TWO independent, competing i18n mechanisms running simultaneously: (1) the correct react-i18next key/value system (useTranslation()/t(), locales/en.ts+es.ts) that 04-08 correctly extended for the floor-facing PM completion and housekeeping depth surfaces; (2) a much older (2026-06-03, commit 5dd25786, 'spanish and strip' -- predates phase 04 by ~7 weeks), completely separate DOM-tree-walking glossary translator (domTranslations.ts) mounted globally via LanguageSync.tsx on every page. This legacy translator uses a TreeWalker to scan literally every text node + certain attributes on the page and does blind regex whole-word substitution (e.g. /\bSchedule\b/gi -> 'Horario', /\bFilter\b/gi -> 'Filtrar') against a large hardcoded PHRASE_TRANSLATIONS/GLOSSARY_TRANSLATIONS dictionary -- with NO distinction between translatable UI copy and raw user-entered data (schedule names, asset names, notes, etc.), and it runs AFTER/independently of React reconciliation, directly mutating the live DOM outside React's control, which is what triggers the hydration-mismatch console error. Confirmed reproducible on a fully fresh dev server restart (ruled out stale-server/HMR caching).
bugs.fix: PARTIALLY FIXED. Added data-i18n-skip="true" to the specific containers rendering raw user data in the phase-04 floor surfaces the orchestrator verified: PMCompletionModal.tsx (dialog root), HousekeepingDepthPanels.tsx (root, covers its children DeepCleanAreasPanel + InspectionDepthPanel), WorkOrderCard.tsx (card body), and pm-schedules/page.tsx (both the mobile-card schedule/asset-name block and the desktop table schedule/asset-name cells). Verified via fresh dev-server restart + Playwright: schedule names like "HVAC Filter Check" no longer get mangled to "HVAC Filtrar Check", and modal titles now render the correct full translation ("Completar programa de PM") instead of a mixed fragment. NOT fixed: a separate, deeper React hydration-mismatch console warning still fires on the pm-schedules page (did not reproduce on /programs) -- this looks like a broader SSR/client i18n-language timing issue (server always renders a default language, client hydrates then swaps to the persisted language) affecting the whole app, not specific to the components this phase touched. Left for a future session to investigate app-wide.

bugs.root_cause: Starlette middleware is LIFO: the LAST middleware registered via app.add_middleware() becomes the OUTERMOST wrapper. main.py registered CORSMiddleware first (innermost) and RateLimitMiddleware second, making RateLimit sit OUTSIDE (in front of) CORS on the request path. RateLimitMiddleware short-circuits with an early 429 JSONResponse WITHOUT calling its own call_next() once a client exceeds its per-route rate limit (10/min on /v1/auth/me, exhausted quickly by real repeated page navigation in a browser session, e.g. multiple dashboard pages each independently checking auth). Because CORS sat inside RateLimit, CORSMiddleware.dispatch() was never entered for that rejected request, so the 429 response left with ZERO Access-Control-* headers. Browsers cannot distinguish "no CORS headers present" from "actual CORS policy violation" and report the same opaque blocked-by-CORS console error for both, so the frontend never even received a readable 429 body — it just saw a network-level failure. Confirmed live: `curl -i -H "Origin: http://localhost:3000" http://localhost:8003/v1/auth/me` after exhausting the limit returned 429 with NO access-control-allow-origin header (SecurityHeadersMiddleware's headers WERE present on the same response, since it sat outside RateLimit and CORS both). This affects every legitimately rate-limited authenticated cross-origin request in production, not just this test.
bugs.fix: Reordered app.add_middleware() calls in main.py so RateLimitMiddleware is registered FIRST (innermost) and CORSMiddleware SECOND, with SecurityHeadersMiddleware remaining last (outermost) — new response path is App -> RateLimit -> CORS -> SecurityHeaders, so CORS (and SecurityHeaders) unconditionally post-process every response including RateLimit's early 429s.
